probe: PLAN R5.2 -- what did the restore_power lottery seeds actually do?
headline: The 0.77/0.00/0.00 spread is largely an argmax artefact, and the hypothesised terminal-gap shortcut is not what the failing seeds do. Sampled on the same ten holdout scenes the three seeds score 10/10, 3/10 and 1/10, not 0. The failing seeds walk to within about one tile of the published gap and then exhaust their poles
method: tools/trace_scenes.py against the three release checkpoints, ten gap_near_drill holdout episodes (3000-3009), both evaluation arms, recording every decision

provenance.checkpoints: restore_power v1.5.0, extractor_version 4, skills action space (23 actions)
provenance.why_a_worktree: these checkpoints cannot run against today's tree: ITEMS grew from 10 to 14 when R4.3 added two families, so the inventory observation is 14 wide where the checkpoint expects 10. The model loads -- SB3 rebuilds input layers from its own pickled space -- but the environment cannot feed it. Probed instead in a git worktree at 3e85950, the last commit before restore_power went to v1.6.0, which is the stack these policies were built for
provenance.holdout: holdout_v2 (the one the release runs cited)
provenance.manifest_git_commit_was_empty: all four archived manifests record an empty git.commit, because the desktop copy was not a git repository when the runs were made. The commit had to be recovered from history by bisecting on the task version -- a provenance gap now closed by making that copy a real clone

cells.published_arm: greedy only -- the release cells record a single structural_success_rate with no stochastic arm

findings: The published zeros are greedy-only. Sampled, seed 2 solves 3 of 10 and seed 3 solves 1 of 10 -- neither is the incapable policy a 0.00 implies.

Under argmax the failing seeds livelock: seed 2 issues place_small_electric_pole_north 1986 times across ten episodes, ~199 of each episode's ~248 decisions, collision-rejected every time. A rejected placement leaves the world unchanged, so the next observation is identical and a deterministic policy repeats it. Same absorbing failure mode found independently on `deliver` the same day.

Sampling breaks the livelock and the error profile inverts: collisions vanish and `no_items` dominates. The failing seeds reach the gap -- median closest approach about one tile -- place poles, and run out.

So the failure is inventory exhaustion near the correct target, not the terminal-gap shortcut restore_power.py hypothesised. That hypothesis predicted the failing policies would target chain interiors; they do not.
Seed 1 is near-perfect when sampled: 10 of 10 in 11-29 decisions, against 8 of 10 under argmax with two 245-decision livelocks.

The seeds differ in placement mechanics rather than targeting: seed 1 and seed 3 place facing south, seed 2 places facing north. Seed 3 also drifts to the generator end of the chain on 3 of 10 scenes.
what_this_closes: R5.2's clause 'confirm policies' actual actions rather than inferring them solely from generator distributions'. The generator-distribution argument inferred a targeting shortcut; the recorded actions contradict it
what_remains: The matched interior/terminal comparison still needs a layout family that places a long chain with both gaps terminal; terminality is currently confounded with chain length in two_gaps.
Multi-fault reaching/fixing/retargeting/completing needs the per-scene progress instrumentation, which does not exist.
limitations: ten scenes per arm per seed, chosen as the first ten of the frozen range rather than sampled -- these are traces, not a scored evaluation, and no rate here should be compared to a published success rate
v1.5.0 stack against holdout_v2, so none of these numbers is comparable to anything measured on today's tree
the probe explains what the policies do, not why they learned it
